class_guess: SO structural counter: binary counter stored between 6-cell-block segments, widening into a finite reservoir
summary: Binary counter over segments of 6-cell blocks; it eats a finite reservoir, and what happens after (~1e13+) is unseen
mechanism: Cycle: from the right edge the head zigzags left (rule Z: 20 steps per block, 101110 -> 111110), bounces off the first boundary that does not carry, then runs right (RS: 6 steps per block). The right edge grows 4 cells per cycle. Halting needs `0 <A 101` (rule H).

The boundaries between block segments hold the bits of a binary counter: which boundary a cycle reaches follows the binary ruler sequence exactly (37,885/37,885 from step 5e4 to 1e10). Segment sizes double per bit (5, 23, 93, 374, 1496, ~6000 blocks at 1e9). Steps 0..~3.6e4 are a different, left-growing counter (init).

The counter grows leftwards into a reservoir (10)^m: m goes 58 -> 11 by step 7.5e9, losing 5 then 2 per new top bit. qsim (block 12): the reservoir is gone by 3.4e12, older prefix gadgets are eaten by 7.7e12, and there is no halt to 8e13. The prefix left after that, 1^4 (01)^11 1 (10)^4, is the open question.

values: qsim: reservoir gone; next gadget (10)^7 down to (10)^2

rules.name: Z  zigzag left (L-pass)
rules.cases: any n >= 0, any context (the head never leaves the shown cells)

rules.name: H  the only way to halt
rules.cases: F1 is the only undefined transition and F is entered only from E0, so every halt goes through this pattern

rules.name: RC3  right end, back to S0, n+1
RC2  right end carries left
rules.cases: X' = X after one deeper pass (bit flips at the boundaries to the left); seen on the orbit, not yet an exact rule

rules.name: D  binary-ruler law for cycle depths
rules.from: cycle k (right record after a leftward excursion > 20 cells)
rules.to: cycles that reach level j+1 are exactly every 2nd cycle that reaches level j
rules.cases: levels found as nested local minima of each cycle's leftmost cell; checked on the real orbit, steps 5e4..1e10 (13 levels); one spacing of 3 at steps 41,783..47,893, the end of the early phase

rules.name: M  reservoir use per new top bit
rules.cases: the 11 consecutive changes 58 -> 53 -> 51 -> ... -> 16 -> 11 on the real orbit (direct, to 1e10); 66 -> 58 at the start does not fit

template.note: Nearest proved machine (3 cells away): a plain BinaryCounter_v2 proof with different words. The class templates SBCv6a/SBCv10/SOBLv1-3 are 8-11 cells away. Longitudinal.v, whose segRLs lemmas SOBLv3 uses (k passes become k*2^len), fits the pass-halving segment structure best.

strategy:
First pin down the epoch map: exact rules for the boundary bit flips and the top gadget, then a fast abstract simulator to watch 2-3 overflows.
Only if the overflows look self-similar: a Longitudinal.v (segRLs) proof with a binary-counter invariant plus an epoch induction.
init covers steps 0..~5e4 (the early left counter).
risks: Halting is decided by the overflow, which has not been seen. After the reservoir and prefix gadgets are gone (~1e13), the counter must reach blank tape on the left and seed a new reservoir, as it did once at step ~3.6e4. Maybe ~1e16 steps, past what qsim reaches.
The inner boundary gadgets (4 states each, in two block phases) and the top gadget are only read off the orbit; RC2, the deep right-end step, has no exact rule.
A proof needs an invariant over an unbounded list of segments plus an epoch-level argument; no template within 2 cells.

checkpoint_questions.text: Fig 2: do the left ends of the orange bars form a binary ruler (every 2nd bar reaches further, every 4th further still, and so on), with no row out of pattern?
Fig 1 and Fig 3: once the left edge stops moving (about a quarter of the way down Fig 1), is every later leftward sweep the 20-step zigzag of Fig 3, followed by a straight run right?

Priority call: the counter eats a finite reservoir (gone by ~3.4e12), then older prefix gadgets (by 7.7e12). Halting depends on the overflow after that, maybe ~1e16 steps out. Should we spend more budget (exact boundary-gadget rules + an abstract simulator to watch overflows), or park this machine?

status_reason: Mechanism found within the current epoch (binary counter over block segments; 6 exact rules validated plus the binary-ruler law at 37,885/37,885). Confidence is low because the long-run overflow (after ~1e13) decides halting and has not been observed. No sign of a cryptid so far.
